baseline.gap: Deployment response sends were CQ-bound, but normal/rejected-client close still blocked the one reactor.

implementation.wire_operation: Existing socket OP_CLOSE 8; exact scalar receipts Started=0 / Unavailable=1 without attachments. Foreign live/unreserved IDs reject. No old denial-as-success fallback.
implementation.owner: OwnedSocket::into_closing consumes the exact socket; ClosingSocket retains accepted PendingCall before OwnedSocket. Existing client phase holds that owner, original deadline and admission-backoff state before submission.
implementation.submission: Only QUEUE_FULL rejection permits another admission attempt; no notification surface exists for it. Accepted close binds to CQ0 and is never resubmitted.
implementation.completion: Started or Unavailable scalar without attachments disarms the logical owner, drops completed pending owner, then returns the client position. Unavailable is an absent full ID below the reservation watermark, with no former-ownership, cleanup, peer, buffer, physical or charge-refund attestation.
implementation.failure: Other submission, binding, wait, service/observation/invalid reply or original expiry aborts with complete scope live. Incomplete ClosingSocket Drop aborts before field destructors, with no wait or second remote close. No cancellation/reconstruction/retry custody.
implementation.shutdown: Existing close operations drain under original budgets while other pools remain live; other pools' older socket destructors remain unqualified blocking contexts.
implementation.ids: Opaque ReservedSocketId consumes one serial at publication, including failed delivery; no reuse within the connection service incarnation. Exhaustion rejects before backend allocation. Packed immediate operations remain a separate full-ID migration gap.
implementation.ownership: C18 extension, no new root, pin, registry, family, recovery owner or physical proof. Close carries no request memory/loan. Unexpected attachments use existing runtime owner cleanup.
remaining: ordinary OwnedSocket close/Drop, including ID restoration and resubmission after accepted-call error, plus other-phase shutdown fallback
general principal/heap accounting and whole-service shutdown latency
